utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. This morning we are proceeding the two of us. Judge Williams is away, and we shall proceed under Rule 15 bis A. The Prosecution is still cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The democratically elected municipality of Bosanski Samac didn't consent -- I'm sorry -- didn't consent to it being taken over, did it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information, but certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not getting a translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You say certainly not. It did not voluntarily surrender its powers to the Serbian municipality, the Serbian Assembly, did it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You say yes. You mean it did not -- you agree with me it did not voluntarily surrender its powers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The democratically elected Assembly, which was operating on the 16th of April, could no longer meet on the 17th or 18th of April, 1992, could it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say yes, you're agreeing with me, that it could no longer meet?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it could no longer meet because the Serbian Assembly had taken over all of its functions, which were now -- the powers of which were concentrated in the hands of the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The takeover -- sorry. This takeover wasn't voluntarily; it was a forcible takeover, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, if it wasn't voluntary from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The takeover was one ethnicity taking over the municipality from -- one ethnicity meaning the Serbs, taking over the municipality from the democratically elected one, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Crisis Staff was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question was: Was a Serb takeover of the municipality, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday you told the Trial Chamber that you didn't agree with discrimination. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you didn't agree with discriminatory practices. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you wouldn't participate in acts of discrimination against other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A provision allowing officials, executives, workers with special privileges and workers in the administration, as well as workers in organisations, institutions, and funds of Serbian ethnicity to retain their status of employee and the rights and duties emerging there from to the final distribution of assets and liabilities - I will show it to him - would be discriminatory, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that some portion of the novel or some other source, or it's exhibit? Because otherwise we don't see any link here. It might be an extract from the newspaper article or from one official --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I don't see reason why to put the witness -- he's not showing this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing wrong with the question. That is the interpretation of the Prosecution and they are entitled to put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You have the question still there on the screen in front of you, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question I asked was: That thing -- that extract I just read to you would be a discriminatory provision, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It gives rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only rights that provision gives is to Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I don't see in this part -- it's page 3 line 12 until 18, I don't see any word with regard to the Serbs. Which Serbs, Serb authorities, Serb people, or what? I mean, we are heading into some very uncertain area, and the witness can be confused with this, Your Honour. Why the Prosecution can simply put the decision or document in front of the witness and then he can make a comment on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is the case of the Prosecution, and they will cross-examine according to the way they understand their case. And the witness is entitled to answer as he understands it, the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only rights that provision gives is to Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rights are given to Serbs, but other ethnicities were also occupying those posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P124.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While it's coming, you know, Mr. Lukic, exactly what provision I'm referring to, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to jog your memory by showing you Article 8 of P2124, which is the decision to establish an assembly of the Serbian people of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, adopted at a joint session, 29th of February, 1992. You've read it now again, refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nowhere in that article does it guarantee the rights -- the employment rights of non-Serb employees, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 8 here states that officials, executives, keep their -- retain their status and their rights until the final distribution of assets and liabilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe I'm misreading the document. Are we reading from the same document, Mr. Lukic? It's Article 8 of the same decision of the 28th of February, 1992, Exhibit P124.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Maybe if the Prosecution could guide which page exactly you're referring to of the Official Gazette. Because it's an Official Gazette. It's a whole document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour excuse me while I get our copy of the exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Maybe the Prosecution can point out which paragraph of Article 8, so that the corresponding one in Serbo-Croat can be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It seems that we are, after all, reading from the same document, as I suspected, Mr. Lukic. Page 4, the right-hand column. Article 8. That was the one you were looking at a moment ago? You're nodding. You mean yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that was the one I read to you a moment ago, a few minutes before I showed it to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that is the one that says: "Officials, executives, workers with special privileges, and workers in the administration, as well as workers in organisations, institutions, and funds of Serbian ethnicity shall retain their status of employee and the rights and duties emerging there from until the final distribution of assets and liabilities."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nowhere in that article does it guarantee the rights and duties or privileges of the status of employment of non-Serb, non-Serbs, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't say that, but it doesn't rule it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It may not rule it out, but it certainly doesn't refer to Muslims, Croats, or other ethnicities, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are not mentioned directly. But they are not excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It specifically guarantees only the rights of people of Serbian ethnicity. Yes or no. Just on what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It guarantees the rights to the Serbian ethnicity, and that's what it says in Article 8. But it does not rule out the possibility of the rights of other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It does not rule -- it does not guarantee the rights of Muslims and Croats in Article 8, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a broader sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So where it says "Serbian ethnicity," we're supposed to read into it "and Muslims and Croats and anyone else," are we?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's the Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Only?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs are Serbian ethnicity, and they are mentioned here, or pointed out here. But this does not exclude other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were Crisis Staff meetings held in April, May, June, and July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the heating plant building, in the socially-owned enterprise Toplana, the heating plant in Samac. And I'm not sure now, but probably one in the agricultural industrial cooperative, the PIK plant. But for the most part, the meetings were held in the heating plant building, outside of the Municipal Assembly building. Because that's where the Crisis Staff had its seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, I think we spoke about this yesterday. You gave some evidence about this yesterday, and you agreed that it had very, very broad powers as the controlling body in the municipality in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It stood in for the Assembly. It had all the powers of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it had powers -- I'm sorry -- its powers -- it derived its powers from authorisation from the government of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I showed you the document yesterday, which was P128, which was the excerpt of the Prime Minister's instruction from the 26th of April, 1992. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be shown P128 again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is P128, it is a document, not an exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have clarification on that? How come it is P128? It wasn't admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Defence opposed admission of this document into evidence until the Prosecution clarified on the chain of custody, and the Prosecution at the time requested that this remain ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: P128, Mr. Lukic, paragraph 2: "The Crisis Staff consists of members each of whom has his own responsibilities, the president, deputy president, commander of the TO, Territorial Defence, staff, president of the executive committee, head of the MUP, Ministry of Interior, and members responsible for the economy, humanitarian and medical care, information and propaganda, procurement and food supplies, refugees, war crimes and damage, communications, coordination, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that, of course, accords with your own experience of the membership of the Crisis Staff and its function in Bosanski Samac, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was a little bit ambiguous when I said your own experience of the membership. Your knowledge, I meant your knowledge of the Crisis Staff and its membership. I'm saying this accords with your knowledge of the Crisis Staff and its membership in Bosanski Samac at that time.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the instructions. I didn't have the opportunity of seeing this excerpt before until now, because according to this, it seems that the government made an instruction, issued an instruction, and then it issued an interpretation of its instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, maybe you misunderstand. I'm only asking you: If what you see there accords with your own knowledge of the membership of the Crisis Staff, that is, if what is written here corresponds with your knowledge of the Crisis Staff in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and according to what I heard, the Crisis Staff was not composed of all of these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, Mr. Lukic: "The Crisis Staff coordinates the functions of authorities in order to ensure the defensive of territories, safety of the population and property, establishment of government and the organisation of all other areas of life and work. In so doing, the Crisis Staff provides the conditions for the municipal executive committee to exercise legal executive authority, run the economy and other areas of life."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that's an accurate summary of the role and powers of the Crisis Staff as you knew it in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should have worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it's clear from that that the Crisis Staff had a wide range of powers; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, or its members, or its membership, had the power to look after public safety, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, public security was provided by the MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Article 2 of this document, the Prime Minister's instruction, says the Crisis Staff consists of various people, including the head of MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Based upon that, the Crisis Staff had -- or its members had authority over public safety, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states in the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff or its members had the power to order the arrest of people; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the law on internal affairs, no, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I said other I said or its members. If the members included the head of MUP, it would have had the power to order arrests; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The head of MUP did. He could have ordered an arrest, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Based on that, a member of the Crisis Staff, or the Crisis Staff, would have had the power to detain, or order detention.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the head of MUP, yes, or rather, he could detain somebody, take somebody into custody and sign the detention order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And of course, the power to establish detention centres.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was regulated at the level of the centre for public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And of course, the power to release detainees.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless somebody files a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And of course, such a member of the Crisis Staff would also have control over the conditions of those in detention; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's his duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And also the power to order the punishment or apprehension of anyone who ill-treated detainees?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because if there is any disturbance of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, of course, also had the power to exchange people who were in detention; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff also had the power to hold people until they were exchanged; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because, of course, there was no higher local authority than the Crisis Staff, was there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That was the highest authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: During 1992 and 1993, the military presence in Bosanski Samac was quite strong, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the military worked with civilian authorities in maintaining order in Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the military performed its military functions, went about its military duties, and if you consider maintaining law and order, then of the recruits.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The military and the civilian authorities, that is, the Crisis Staff, worked together in maintaining law and order in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each in his own field of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, according to the order of the Prime Minister of the 26th of April, 1992, was required to coordinate, according to paragraph 3, the functions of authorities to ensure the defensive territories, the safety of population and property.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've already agreed with me that paragraph 3 reflects, as far as you're concerned, what was happening in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I said to you a moment ago, the effective of this, and its reflection upon what was actually happening in Bosanski Samac, was that the military and civilian authorities were working together to maintain law and order in Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each in his own field, domain. The civil authorities for the civilian population and the military authorities for the conscripts. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And according to Article 3 of that excerpt, under the coordination of the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday you gave evidence that you knew that there were 300 -- some 300 Croats and Muslims detained in the two schools.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you also said that you were aware of prisoners being detained in the SUP and TO building; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building of the Territorial Defence, yes, and in the secondary school building as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The population of Bosanski Samac was about 6.000; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5.500, the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Some 300 people would represent maybe 5 per cent of the population, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was obvious that there had been mass arrests in Bosanski Samac in April, May 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And mass arrests could only have been ordered by the civilian or military authorities, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were civilians, then the civilian authorities; and if they were conscripts, then the military authorities or military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The civilian authorities were, of course, under the coordination and control of the Crisis Staff, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if, through the ministry of the department, it had not been regulated otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So mass arrests of civilians in Bosanski Samac could only have been ordered by the Crisis Staff or its members; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the public security station could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The head of the public security station was a member of the Crisis Staff, the mass arrests could only have been ordered by the Crisis Staff or its members; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the head of the public security station who was a member, because according to the payroll, the list for salaries, I didn't see his name on it, although I did hear that he boasted around town that he was indeed a member of the Crisis Staff. That's what he said around town. But I wasn't in the Crisis Staff myself, so I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you're referring, of course, to Stevan Todorovic, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the head of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The mass arrest of 300 civilians could not have occurred without the Crisis Staff knowing about it, could it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I heard about it, then I'm sure that the Crisis Staff must have heard about it as well, heard about it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you had heard about 300 civilians -- Croat and Muslim civilians being detained in the schools, then the Crisis Staff would also have heard about it. The same applies to other detention centres, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If civilians were being detained at Crkvina or Zasavica, the Crisis Staff would have had to have known about it, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If 16 Croats had been massacred in a warehouse in Crkvina, the Crisis Staff would have had to have been aware of it, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it, so they would have had to have heard about it, or they should have informed themselves along those lines about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was common knowledge in Bosanski Samac that large numbers, hundreds of civilians, were being detained, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were rumours going around to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There were articles published in the papers, and there were announcements on the radio when people were arrested; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the radio in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, the radio in Samac. There were announcements on the radio in Samac periodically when people were arrested, such as so-and-so has been arrested on suspicion of holding weapons in his house.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information of that kind, because the radio worked very infrequently, and I rarely listened to the radio anyway. So I can't confirm that, whether it was broadcast over Radio Samac or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You agreed yesterday that the detention, without trial or charge, was unlawful under the Republika Srpska constitution, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In conformity with the Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And anyone who was detained should have been brought before a court and charged and tried with an offence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the procedure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The 300 people or so who were detained in the elementary schools -- sorry - the three schools in Bosanski Samac - were not brought before any court or charged with any offences, were they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the commander of the public security station, the komandir, I heard about the individuals who were concerned, the number of persons and that an investigation was underway against them. But I do not know how this investigation was concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You certainly heard no reports of court proceedings related to 300 people who were arrested and detained in the schools in Bosanski Samac, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive any information of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And as far as you know, your information at the time was that these people were detained only because they were Croats and Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, yes. There were Croats and Muslims there too, but the report was that they had been detained because of certain activities. Now, whether because this was -- because they had weapons in their possession or because they were preparing an armed uprising. That was the information I received from the commander when I talked to him about the persons who these charges were being brought against.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But what was Stevan Todorovic's reputation in 1992 and 1993 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't socialise with him at all, had no contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He was the chief of police, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He was going around town saying he was on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I don't know whether to everybody, but he did go around bragging about that and talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm asking you what was his reputation. You said yesterday that as far as you knew he and Dr. Simic didn't get on very well. What was his reputation? Why didn't they get on?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was more a cafe-going type of man, who liked to live freely, loosely. He didn't have a family. And for many years he was doing his studies at university. He studied a long time. That's what I could say about him character-wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, he had a reputation for violence in the town at the time, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I got information along those lines even from members of the military, especially those who communicated with me, connected to the materiel and equipment for the army, the financial side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have a few minutes' break to get some papers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Get papers from where?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: From my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you remember yesterday you were supposed to wind up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am well on the way to winding up. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a ten minutes' break and resume at 10.30. --- Break taken at 10.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before our break, I was asking you about Stevan Todorovic's reputation, and you said you had information about his reputation for violence from members of the military who communicated it to you. His reputation for violence was of someone who was mistreating prisoners in custody; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard, but from the people who came back after 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: His reputation for violence included killing people in custody, didn't it, the murder of detainees?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard. I heard that from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that was something that was rumoured in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993, wasn't it, that Todorovic was responsible for mistreating and even killing prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't want to claim that it was rumoured that he had killed any prisoners --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as far as I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was rumoured in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993 that Stevan Todorovic had mistreated prisoners, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something along those lines from Commander Savo Cancarevic, that he went in there, he would go in there, usually during the night, and that the duty officers, policemen on duty, told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday I asked you about the Vidovdan award, which you were awarded on the 30th of June, 1993, and you agreed, and it was published in the gazette, that on that day, you shared a Vidovdan, St. Vitus day award with Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Stevan Todorovic, for "the selfless contribution to the struggle for freedom and the defence of Republika Srpska." Now, I'm just putting to you that that's what was in the gazette that you looked at yesterday. If you want to have a look at it again, you can.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no need. I received the Vidovdan award, St. Vitus Day award, for contributing to the economy and social issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the award --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But so did the other people, the names of -- you read out. I don't know what field they received the award for.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The gazette of your decoration, and it's called a decoration, is for selfless contribution to the struggle for freedom and the defence of Republika Srpska. That's what it says, doesn't it? That's a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But we did go through this yesterday. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Only in one respect, Your Honour. It was right at 7.00, and there were just several other things on this I just wished to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you're concluding?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Almost, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what Milan Simic's selfless contribution to struggle for freedom in the defence of Republika Srpska was, that entitled him to this decoration.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the decision to award the decoration, the reasons are stipulated for which the award is given, and the decoration is given by the Municipal Assembly. I can't remember -- I can't say for certain what it said on his document, the award that he received.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you can't tell the Trial Chamber what Milan Simic "selfless contribution to the struggle for freedom in the defence of Republika Srpska" is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think that is a fair question to this witness, because he did explain even yesterday that it was within the purview of those people making the decision. So I don't think this is a fair question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph Exhibit P14-43 and 14-46 and 14-56.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The photograph you're showing, I just want to identify for the Trial Chamber. That is in fact a photograph of the police station, the white building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the building immediately to its left is the Municipal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And which is of course where your offices were in 1992 and 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the building on the right, the police station, is that the one where you heard the prisoners singing the Serbian songs, Serbian national songs, coming from?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left, across the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The building across the road. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the next photograph, which is P46.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that another view of the Municipal Assembly building, right next to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And can the witness please be shown the other photograph there, which is P -- is it 56?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a photograph of the back of the police station, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Showing the garages?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And immediately to the left, on the top left-hand side is a building which is part of the Municipal Assembly building; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's one photo which I forgot to mention, P14A-50. Can that also be shown to the witness, please. The photograph on the screen now, that's of the territorial -- or the TO headquarters, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that's the building from where you heard the sounds of Muslim and Croat prisoners singing Serbian national songs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that was diagonally opposite where you were working, maybe 50 metres away?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if prisoners were being tortured and mistreated such as to cause them to scream out loudly in pain, you would have been able to hear that from the street in that building, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't that far that you wouldn't be able to hear that. You could hear the singing also.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And in the first few months after the takeover, April, May, June 1992, you could hear people screaming out loudly from that building in front of you, and the police station across the road, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, because I didn't hear the screams, except for the singing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In May 1996, there was public meeting in -- organised by the SDS in Bosanski Samac, which you attended, to assure the people of Bosanski Samac for their support of "all our so-called war criminals"; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There was a public meeting held, which you attended, in your capacity as mayor of Bosanski Samac, in support of Karadzic and Mladic, in May 1996, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, what has that got to do with the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It goes to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it correct, 1996?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. It goes to the credibility of the witness, Your Honour, and any bias he may have, having been brought as a Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Briefly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was among the first to participate in the voluntary surrender of our fellow citizens to The Hague Tribunal. These were the first persons to voluntarily surrender to The Hague Tribunal from Republika Srpska, and I don't know how I could not recognise or negate The Hague Tribunal or be against it, because as a lawyer I understand and I know what a public indictment means. I remember that meeting, and I can tell you what I said, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Lukic, please tell us what you said on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you could, so please could you tell us what you said on that day.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that day. It wasn't organised by the SDS. It was a spontaneous gathering of citizens throughout Republika Srpska. A few citizens came to my office and told me that a large group of people had gathered in front of the hotel, and they asked me to go and to address that group. I asked them what was the reason that that group of people gathered together. They told me that there were many people there from Odzak and Orasje. And the reason was a piece of information that arrived relating to the issuance of public indictments. I, as president of the Assembly, went there. I don't usually like to speak much, and I did say a few sentences, and I can interpret what I said. I know that you are not satisfied, just like myself, because only Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic are on this public indictment, and that also Alija Izetbegovic and Franjo Tudjman are not there as well, and their generals. But believe me, we will fight through the institutions of the system for their names to be placed there too, so that they can then prove what the real truth was. Then I mentioned the names of our accused as well and told them, "I know why you are angry, because of what happened to you in Odzak and Orasje, but we will endeavour that the names on that other side too are nominated to The Hague Tribunal through the institutions of the system." After that -- that was the end of my speech. After that, at the end of 1996 and in 1997, I directly participated in conversations with the investigators from The Hague Tribunal, and I took part in all the negotiations or conversations relating to the surrender of our fellow citizens to The Hague Tribunal. So it's impossible for anyone to say that I am against that Tribunal. Let me also say that at the level of the government and the group that was tasked with investigating the victims from the other side, I strived for us to show proof for the suffering of the Serbian people from the other two ethnic groups, because that is the only way for us to show what the real truth is. That was my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Let's move to another question now. Since you have been in the municipality as an official for many years and you're a lawyer by profession, what are the competencies of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on local self-management and administration determines the competencies of the Municipal Assembly, and they are social policy, urban affairs, regulatory plan, communal policy, infrastructure, education, the part that pertains to material expenditures for high schools, setting up of hospitals, medical centres, and preschool facilities. Those are the main duties. And as far as the economy is concerned, it deals with that part of it which deals with state capital or socially owned property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the period before 1992, and also the period from 1992 until now, and if there's any difference, please tell us so. My question is as follows. Please listen to my question. Is it -- did anybody of these municipal officials, in accordance with the legal regulations, were they able to command military units?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the exclusive duty of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But not at the municipal level?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next question: Did anyone from the municipal government have the right to command police units?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The use of police units is ordered by the minister, an order for such activities is issued by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which minister?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can any municipal official issue orders for a person to be detained, under the valid rules and regulations?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A detention order can only be issued by the criminal investigation service in the public security station and the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. Firstly, it doesn't arise from cross-examination; and secondly, the questions I asked of the witness were directed to the powers of the Crisis Staff, not municipal officials, then or now. I can't see how it can arise from anything I asked in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's obvious. It arose many times. My learned friend make various parallel approaches between Municipal Assembly and Crisis Staff, municipal administration and Crisis Staff. So my next question is directly related to that, but I have to make this introduction. So we are hearing here for almost two hours this structure between municipal authorities and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but -- yes, but it was related to the membership of the chief of police in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now I'm heading to these areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please avoid what wasn't raised in cross-examination, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now, please, could you tell me the following, even though you talked about this already when I questioned you a few days ago: What does the Crisis Staff represent? What kind of a body is it? Who does it substitute for?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff is an institution which, in extraordinary circumstances, or during times of war, stands in for the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have certain lines. I just want to reorganise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many citizens did the municipality of Bosanski Samac have, if you know, according to the census from 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: According to the 1991 census, how many inhabitants did the municipality of Bosanski Samac have?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Bosanski Samac, according to the census from 1991, had 32.700 inhabitants. Out of that, 45 per cent were Croats, 43 per cent Serbs, 5 per cent Muslims, and the others were Yugoslavs, Montenegrins, and those who declared themselves differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the town itself had how many inhabitants, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 5.500 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the information that there were a couple of hundred of detained persons, does this apply to the entire territory of Bosanski Samac, the entire municipality, or does it apply only to the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applies to the entire territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As a lawyer, as a man from that profession, when there is a pre-criminal procedure and when there is a founded suspicion that a criminal act was committed, can the police issue a detention order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if the suspicions prove founded, can the investigative judge issue a detention order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to 30 days, or up to six months at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: According to the then laws, that were then in force, how long did the investigation have to continue? When did it have to be completed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on the qualification of the criminal act and the severity of the sentence that can be passed, so I cannot respond to that specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about armed rebellion, unauthorised possession of weapons, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what prison sentence is planned for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about detention, Mr. Lukic. Is detention provided for in the period of one month, two months, three months? Do you perhaps remember the length of detention?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember. I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is your understanding of the term "coordination"? Does coordination also mean an order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There should be a difference between being informed and reporting. The superior officer is -- he is reported to, and a person who was the role of a coordinator is somebody who provides information or informs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we take our break? 11.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll come back at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, Mr. Lukic, I asked you a question. Just let me see what it was. The answer wasn't very clear, so I'll repeat it. Could you please explain to us, if you can, between the verb "to coordinate" and "to order," what your understanding of those two verbs is.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that "to order" implies that you are subordinate, in the sense that the subordinated person submits a report, or reports back to his superior. And "to coordinate" is a looser form, and in that form, somebody informs someone of something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the Prosecutor asked you about the fact that -- on the basis of the knowledge that you had about certain detainees, did you assume that the Crisis Staff could have known about that too? Or let me put it this way: You learnt from Savo Cancarevic -- what did you learn about the foundations for detaining those persons from Savo Cancarevic, the reason for their detention? What did Savo Cancarevic actually tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this. This was covered in examination and cross-examination. The same answer was given both times. Nothing requires clarification, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It requires, Your Honour, because I have to find out -- we have to find out here what the alleged knowledge and to what extent, to which extent, might be with regard to certain informations within the Crisis Staff, and that's the line of my questioning, simple as that. Because that was raised in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I will allow the question. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you this: What did the commander of the police, komandir, said was the basis for having these people detained? What did Savo Cancarevic tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that some persons had been taken into detention because they were found in possession of military weapons, and some persons had been detained because there were indications to show that they were involved in preparing an armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that the Crisis Staff had this same type of information with respect to the grounds for detaining these people?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the chief of police informed them about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now a few words about the exchanges. Which body was in charge of the exchange process?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A commission was set up for exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there any higher level body above the municipal level in charge of this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a republican commission. I don't know its exact title.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there a commission within the framework of the military organs perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about a military commission that was in existence, and I think that the commission was headed by Mr. Grujo -- I think his first name was Grujo. I can't remember his surname. Or maybe Grujic. Grujo or Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In keeping with the rules and regulations in force at the time, who could have ordered a person to be released from detention?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who detained the individual in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you be a little more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If an individual was a civilian and had been detained by the public security station, then that same person could have been released by that same body, that is to say, the public security station, on its own or in cooperation with the prosecutor. If we're dealing with a military person, then it would be the military body and military prosecutor, under whose competence it was to do the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you were asked by the Prosecutor -- actually, he asked you a number of questions relating to Cadre's policy at the municipal level in the period after the multiparty elections had taken place in 1990. What I'm asking you now is this: What personal knowledge do you have about the following fact, which three parties had political power and authority, or rather, had the coalition at a republican level, at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Assembly and the government, to the best of my knowledge, were represented by -- or consisted of the representatives of the Croatian Democratic Union, the Party of Democratic Action, and the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, this coalition government, was it reflected on a local, municipal level at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were local elections, and the vote was similar. The outcome of the vote reflected that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about what the outcome of the vote was, but who de facto had the political coalition in the Samac municipality after the elections in 1990. Just briefly. Don't waste too much time on that, please. Keep it brief.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HDZ, the SDA, and the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So on that basis, was there a distribution of posts, functions, in the local municipal administration?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question -- or rather, the Prosecutor's next question related to the concept of representatives or deputies in parliament in the parliament of Republika Srpska, and he touched upon the decision whereby Dr. Blagoje Simic and Mr. Mirko Dragic were appointed as representatives. So a very concrete question: Of the three categories, that is to say, a member of parliament, MP, a representative or observer, which of those concepts can be applied to this situation referring to Dr. Blagoje Simic and Mirko Dragic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Observer status.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the following: When the conflict broke out in mid-April 1992, in Bosanski Samac -- Mr. Lukic, shall I -- may I assist you? Don't look at the transcript, because it's in English. It will take away your concentration. Just listen to my questions. Listen to me. You'll find it easier, I think. And my question is this: In mid-April 1992, was the primary school in Bosanski Samac damaged in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 20th of April, I think, it was set fire to, or rather, a shell hit it, and the entire roof burnt down, so that it wasn't used. It wasn't used at all right up until 1998, when, with the assistance of international donors, the European Union, and along with the involvement of 1.500.000 German marks, we were able to repair the damage and put the building right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the academic year in Samac ended? Give us a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know why it was interrupted, the academic year was interrupted?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that's when it would have come to an end anyway. It was the end of the year, school year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you the following question: Bearing in mind the circumstances in Samac from April onwards, was it possible to ensure tuition for the children, safely?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said something about that. Many children didn't go to school at all. They didn't turn up for classes. So that probably that was the reason for the ministry to decide to declare the school year terminated for that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Samac shelled in April, May 1992? Just say yes or no. Give us a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Under these circumstances, could it have been possible for children to attend school normally? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another question from the Prosecutor: That you said two schools in Samac, from April to October 1992, were full of Muslims and Croats, detainees. What I'm asking you now is this: You told us what you knew about the detainees in April. Now, can you tell me, in this connection, in connection with the detainees in school, were they there in April, in the month of April? Were there any detainees in the school house?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any in May?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For orientational purposes, did you perhaps receive any information from Savo Cancarevic how many of them there might have been in May, how many detainees in May? Were there, say, 50, a hundred, 150, 300, or a thousand?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many exactly, but the number was far smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Less than a hundred?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know of an exchange that took place in the presence of the International Red Cross between the Odzak side and the Samac side?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In what period did this take place?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In October 1991, in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was outvoting that took place on the Croatian and Muslim side; rather, they outvoted the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked no questions at all about the processes in the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina parliament before the takeover. That's completely outside the scope of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There are some relations, but okay, I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo was being established when exactly?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In February 1992, were there any representatives of the Serb sides in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina formed, or rather, the Republika Srpska? When was that formed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was after the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And when was the plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In October or November of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about the National Assembly of Republika Srpska? Was it functioning at that time, and was it making decisions?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Republika Srpska, was it the legal, lawful, and legitimate subject at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. This witness is here as a fact witness for what happened in Bosanski Samac, not as a constitutional expert as to the legitimacy or otherwise of the declaration of the Republika Srpska or the government organs at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the same time, Your Honour, if I may, my learned friend asked this witness about the fact of the internationally recognition and all other issues, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The question was: Was it recognised by this entity or that entity. It wasn't whether was the recognition valid. That wasn't the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But he mentioned EU and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the Americans.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- USA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just the recognition, not whether that recognition was valid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I take this ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were saying -- my next question: Explain to the Court, please, why the Republika Srpska was established in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again I object. It's outside the scope of re-examination. I didn't ask any questions relating to the establishment of Republika Srpska or the reasons. This trial is about persecution on a local level in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's even more important is that that wasn't raised in cross-examination, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for the establishment of the Serb municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A recommendation by the National Assembly of the Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And is that municipality a component part of Republika Srpska to this day?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is Republika Srpska recognised as an entity under the Dayton Agreement?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The big powers at Dayton, the superpowers at Dayton, drew up the Dayton Agreement, along with the presence of the representatives of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just tell me yes or no: Was it recognised as an entity or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was a decision made by which Republika Srpska would remain within Yugoslavia at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people stated their views at the plebiscite, voted on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who was the legal military formation in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When asked by the Prosecutor, you said that on the 18th of April, 1992, in Samac, that JNA soldiers patrolled the streets of Samac. Were they soldiers who had been mobilised or were they the local population or were they soldiers who had come in from outside from Yugoslavia itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers who had been mobilised from the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, 1992, was there -- was it legal and normal for members of the JNA to be on the territory of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this. Again it's outside this witness's -- it's outside cross-examination and outside the scope of this witness's expertise. He's a fact witness, not one as to the constitutional division between Yugoslavia and Bosnia at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I just read a question of my learned friend? Unfortunately, I don't have pages here. It was 17 hours 25: How do you say that the JNA soldiers had not taken over the town and replaced the democratically elected municipality with its own. So my question, Your Honour, is here in order to clarify that issue. And that issue was raised yesterday with regard to the JNA, legality, how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Not the legality. It was a fact question. They were democratic elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: According to your personal knowledge, on the 18th of April, 1992, was there a takeover of power in Samac by the army? Did the JNA take control in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on that particular day I saw our army out in the streets, or rather, the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there a takeover of power by them in Samac on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you personally, or did you happen to hear it rumoured in the time before mid-April 1992, did you have any information about the presence of enemy military forces around Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already testified to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please tell me whether you knew this or did not.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what forces were these?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were representatives of the Croatian army on our territory, on the territory of our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any other military forces there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there talk of any military operations and indeed an attack on Samac by those forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What kind of rumours were these? What forces were supposed to attack Samac? Who was supposed to attack Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this, Your Honour. The witness testified in examination, examination-in-chief, that he had heard rumours, and it rose to no more than the level of rumours that there were Croats forces nearby. I didn't ask him about Croat forces in the territory except to say there weren't any, and he agreed there were none there. My learned friend is now putting to the witness again the same rumours as if to elevate them to the level of fact. In my submission, the witness can take it no further and it doesn't arise from cross-examination. He has no personal knowledge. He made it quite clear in cross-examination and in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The fact is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The fact is there were rumours, hearsay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is, so and that has been said by the witness and that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, then: What was your conclusion, although you're not a military expert, but you're an educated man. What did you think the JNA units were doing there composed of the local inhabitants, in that period from around the 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the witness is not here to tell us what he thinks they were doing. He's a fact witness. If he knows, that's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know what they were doing, what the JNA troops were doing, composed of the local population around April 1992 in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were supposed to prevent an armed uprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the Croatian forces, the Croatian and Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How did you come to learn this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard it in town, that story, or rather, that information, was something that was shared by all other inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P89, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, just one question: How long did the mandate of the Crisis Staff last, in terms of time? If it was established in April, how long did it go on for?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of July or beginning of August, the War Presidency was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that means how long did the Crisis Staff last?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of April, May, June, and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And how long did the War Presidency go on for? How long was that in existence?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the first assembly was held, and the first assembly was held sometime in mid-December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So from December 1992, which body was functioning in the territory of Samac municipality, in the political sense?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this document now, please. The Prosecutor asked you about the preamble of this document. Could you please interpret it for me, particularly in terms of which paramilitary formations were meant here, the ones that are included in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croat Muslim ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know any names maybe of those formations?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zengas, Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, usher. Now I would like to discuss this war tax issue, very briefly, Exhibit P102, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at Article 3, please. Does Article 3 refer to persons -- does Article 3 refer to persons who have a regular work permit abroad, or does it refer to some other persons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that those who have regular papers abroad, from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just concentrate on Article 3, please. I'm asking you specifically: Is there any mention here of people who do not have a work permit in Article 3?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me the following: How do you interpret this "All persons living abroad and have not been issued with valid work or residence permits"? So does this then refer to people who do not have valid foreign work permits? We have two categories. One category are those who have work permits, and the other category, those who do not have it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not refer to those who do not possess a working visa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If they do not have a valid work permit for some European country, what was their duty, according to some republican regulations? You talked about that yesterday, so could you please explain that a little more.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since general mobilisation was called, they were obliged to report to the -- they were obliged to report to the mobilisation call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that meant that they were obliged to come back and place themselves at the disposal of the competent authorised command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To return to the country and to make themselves available to the Defence Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the second category are persons who have a work permit, a foreign work permit. Did they also have the obligation to come back and place themselves at the disposal of the Defence Ministry?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was their duty, if there was any, that they had, in times of war, in terms of a war duty?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To pay the wartime tax, or to pay -- i.e., to pay an additional income tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: De facto, in the course of 1992 and 1993, what was the ethnicity of the persons who came back on work or holiday or some other -- for some other reason to the Samac municipality? What was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it already. Most of them, or in percentages, 99 per cent, were Serbs, and 1 per cent were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When Serbs came to their town and visited their relatives, they were obliged to pay that tax because they would then receive a kind of receipt or a certificate based on that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be given a form stating that they were obliged to pay this tax, and then they would be given a kind of receipt stating that they had paid this tax.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, all this was given yesterday. We are simply repeating. Re-examination does not mean repeating what was already discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I will narrow the issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
